questiontext.text:
Goal

A museum display card identifies an exhibit and describes its recorded value. The curator also wants each card to show the value's Go type, so a count cannot be mistaken for a mass.

Read
  • fmt, the Printing section. Check the verb list at the top. Which verb prints a value's type? Which verb prints a string as it would appear in a Go file?
  • fmt, the same section. Find the float row in the table headed The default format for %v. Find the paragraph about precision. What precision does %g use when none is specified?
  • fmt, the paragraph naming the four printing families. Which family adds a newline? Does Printf belong to that family?
Coming from Java

A Java developer might use String.format, type quote marks around %s, and call System.out.println for the newline. Java's %s does not escape the string. Java has no formatting verb for a value's type.

System.out.println(String.format("Count: %d", count));
System.out.println("Title: \"" + title + "\"");
Banned: Println. Required: %T
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Two verbs in the Printing section mention Go syntax. Read both and choose the verb for a string.
  • Find default format and read the row for float types. Also read the paragraph about precision.

expected.text: East wing: "Rosetta Stone" Count: 1 Mass: 760.5 float64
West wing: "Terracotta Warriors" Count: 8 Mass: 150.25 float64

name.text: WAT 06.2: A Rune with a View!

questiontext.text:
Goal

A hotel charges for engraving each letter of a guest's name on a brass door plate. The invoice for Zoë Müller is wrong. Fix the billing program.

Read
  • Strings, bytes, runes and characters in Go, the section What is a string. What does a string contain?
  • The same article, Printing strings. Find the byte-by-byte loop and the following sentence. What does a string index access? What does the loop's len limit count?
  • The same article, Range loops. What two values does each iteration produce? What does the first value count?
Coming from Java

In Java, length() and indexOf both appear to operate on letters. Go's len and string indexes use a different unit.

int letters = name.length();
int at = name.indexOf('M');
Banned: utf8, RuneCountInString
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Find the sentence in Range loops that defines the loop index. Can you use that index as the letter position?
  • Find the sentence in Printing strings that defines a string index. What does len count instead?

Goal

A signwriter builds banners from many pieces of text. The old program joins one piece at a time and takes all day. Write a faster version that builds each banner as one strip without using glue. spaced puts one space between neighbouring letters and none at either end, and É counts as one letter. underlined writes the word, a newline, then one dash for each letter, so É earns one dash. marquee joins the copies as the example shows and also returns the strip's length in bytes, so É counts twice there.

Read
  • strings.Builder. Read the type documentation and its method list. What setup does a Builder need before the first write? Which methods accept a string, a rune, and a byte?
  • Builder.Len. Read its sentence. What does Len count? According to the final equation, what does that count equal?
  • Builder.WriteRune. Read both sentences. What does WriteRune append? What does its first return value count?
Coming from Java

A Java developer might use new StringBuilder(), chain append calls, and finish with toString(). Another option is plain + inside a loop. Go's Builder has none of those methods, and the red line bans +.

StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
for (char c : word.toCharArray()) sb.append(c).append(' ');
return sb.toString().trim();
Banned: +, Sprintf. Required: strings.Builder
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Read the third sentence of the Builder documentation before looking for a constructor.
  • Apply the equation at the end of Len's sentence to CAFÉ before writing marquee.

testcode.text: fmt.Println(marquee("CAFÉ", 2)) s, n := marquee("CAFÉ", 0) fmt.Printf("%q %d\n", s, n)
